title: The Knight on the Rim
setup: White's knight was chased to a3 in the opening and has done nothing since. Black's pawns cover its exits. Start it on a better route.
hint: List every square that knight can legally use, then cross off the ones a black pawn already attacks.
explanation:
## The Idea

The knight on a3 is White's worst piece. Black's pawns take its forward squares away: b5 is defended by the a-pawn and c4 is covered by the b-pawn, and going home to b1 only undoes a move.

{{Nc2}} is not a retreat but the first leg of a route: c2, then e3, where it supports the knight on d5. Black gets on with {{Bg5}}, and White walks the next leg with {{Nce3}}.

Which piece is doing the least, where would it rather stand, and what is the shortest road there?
